params.body:
Three open Western sources, free and allowed for commercial use, while Reddit stays off by its own policy and TikTok and Instagram stay rented.

- **YouTube, wider and with comments.** Most popular videos in ten countries instead of six (ES, IT, PL and SE added; Europe first). For videos in the categories where young audiences talk back (music, gaming, people & blogs, comedy, entertainment, howto & style), up to four per country, the five most relevant comments go into the signal as text: what a video meant to the people watching it. No names, no channel ids. Same key, within the free quota.
- **Bluesky trending** (`bluesky-trends`): the public trending topics, no account. Topic level only: name, description, category, post count; the accounts are not kept. Searching posts needs a signed-in account (403), so it does not search.
- **Wikipedia spikes** (`wikipedia-spikes`): per language (nl, fr, de, es, it, pl, sv, en), articles that jumped into yesterday's top 200 and were not in the top 1000 a week earlier, ten per language. Wikimedia pageviews API with a descriptive User-Agent.

Tried live on 2 October: Bluesky 25 topics (mostly US politics and tech), Wikipedia 175 jumps before the cap (mostly television and news names). Both are weak for youth culture on their own; the classifier's relevance filter decides what stays. Both count as observed evidence under the Standard (`otherwise: observed`).

The two source rows are seeded on the first collect (INSERT OR IGNORE, so a row switched off by hand stays off). 997 tests pass.
params.title: Sources: three open Western sources
